effects.target: An invisible spirit occupies your space; when a creature makes an attack of opportunity against you it attacks using your base attack bonus plus your Dexterity modifier, and on a hit that attack of opportunity automatically misses. effects.target: Creates 1d4 + your caster level floating scout eyes: Fine constructs with 1 hp, AC 18, fly 30 feet, +20 Fly, +16 Stealth and a Perception modifier equal to your caster level (maximum +15), each seeing 120 feet by normal vision. You give them one instruction of 25 words or fewer; an eye must return to your hand to replay what it saw, at 1 round per hour recorded, and then vanishes. An eye that gets more than 1 mile from you ceases to exist.

prying-eyes.notes: Creation/scouting; the vocabulary has no summon or remote-sensing type. The 1 hp, AC 18 and skill bonuses belong to the created eyes, not to the caster, so none of them are emitted as effects.

effects.target: As a swift action you retreat into a personal mindscape for up to 15 minutes while no time passes for your body, then continue your turn. Inside you can recall with perfect clarity any text, conversation or image you were exposed to within the past 1 week per caster level, and you may use the time to prepare a single spell. Mind-affecting effects already on you continue to expend their duration while you are inside; other effects on your body do not.

psychic-asylum.notes: The 15 minutes are subjective time inside the mindscape; the spell itself is instantaneous, so the stated duration is the one emitted.

Mind-affecting effects that hit the image affect you fully whenever your mind occupies it. The spell ends if you cross to another plane.

A target with a heavier condition is treated as having the lesser one instead for the duration: blinded becomes dazzled, exhausted becomes fatigued, frightened becomes shaken, nauseated becomes sickened. When the spell ends, the original conditions apply again in full if they are still running.

recentering-drone.notes: Ignoring a condition's penalties is exactly suppress_condition, so the four light conditions convert cleanly. Downgrading one condition to a lesser one has no type - suppressing blinded outright would be stronger than the spell, so the table is narrated.

effects.target: You regain one use of every 0-level and 1st-level spell-like ability you have from a racial trait.

recharge-innate-magic.notes: Restores uses of an ability; the vocabulary has no resource-recovery type.

While further away than 30 feet it is staggered, until it is near the object of its desire again. If staying within 30 feet would put it in obvious physical danger it may attempt a second save to break the spell.

reckless-infatuation.notes: The staggered condition is conditional on the target's position rather than applied on a failed save, so it is described inside the narrative instead of being an apply_condition that would stagger the target from the moment of casting. Counters unadulterated loathing.

effects.target: will
effects.note: the saving throw is the firearm's, as an object; the effect lands on whoever wields or carries it

effects.target: The firearm discharges by itself even when unloaded. If it was loaded, that ammunition is wasted.

recoil-fire.notes: The prone alternative depends on the wielder's existing state, which no branch of a save gate can test, so it rides in the note.

effects.target: disguise
effects.note: only on checks to impersonate the individual whose corpse was used

The focus item must stay within 30 feet of the target or the spell ends and the flesh sloughs away.

The disguise is very hard to detect: the target sheds no magical aura under detect magic (the focus item radiates strong necromancy instead), true seeing does not reveal its true form, and detect undead reads it as undead although it is not and is not affected by anything else that targets undead. Alignment is not disguised. If the target dies the spell continues, and raise dead or similar restores the target rather than the corpse; the corpse itself can only be restored by miracle, resurrection, true resurrection or wish. Can be made permanent by a 15th-level caster with permanency and a 17,500 gp material component.

recorporeal-incarnation.notes: Printed duration is 1 WEEK per level; the duration unit vocabulary stops at 'day', so it is written as 7 days per level - an exact conversion, not a guess. A 'week' unit would be the cleaner fix.

effects.target: will
effects.note: the save is made by the killer of the corpse you used as a focus, wherever they are, not by anyone you can see

on_failure.target: The killer's right hand is stained indelibly red and the stain cannot be removed, though it can be hidden by gloves or by magic such as disguise self. A killer with no right hand gets a hand-shaped red stain elsewhere, usually the chest.

effects.target: Affects only the creature that directly killed the corpse - accomplices are untouched, and a victim who did not die by violence or died indirectly leaves the spell with no effect at all. Distance does not matter but the killer must be on your plane, and a corpse can only ever serve as the focus once.

red-hand-of-the-killer.notes: The target of the save is a creature the caster has never seen and may be a world away; nothing in the schema says who a save_gate is aimed at, so the note carries it.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: granted to whoever wears the enchanted hat in the head slot, not to the caster

effects.target: The wearer regains 1d4 hit points whenever they deal the killing blow to a living creature.

redcap-s-touch.notes: The 1d4 is triggered healing on a killing blow, not healing at casting - a heal spec would restore 1d4 the moment the hat is enchanted, so it is narrated. The +2 has no stated bonus type, hence untyped.

As reduce person, on a single willing animal: it drops one size category, halving height, length and width and dividing weight by 8. Reduce the damage of the animal's natural attacks for its new size.

reduce-animal.notes: Numbers taken from reduce person, which this spell says it functions like. No save gate: the target must be willing and the spell's own save line is 'none'.

effects.target: fort

The humanoid halves in height, length and width and its weight divides by 8, dropping one size category; speed is unchanged. A Small target reduced to Tiny has a 2-1/2 foot space and 0 natural reach, so it must enter an opponent's square to attack; a Large target reduced to Medium has a 5-foot space and 5-foot reach. Carried equipment shrinks with it and melee and projectile weapons deal less damage, but any reduced item that leaves the creature's possession instantly returns to normal size - so thrown weapons deal normal damage. Size-reducing effects do not stack. Counters and dispels enlarge person, and can be made permanent with permanency.

reduce-person.notes: The attack and AC bonuses are typed size because the prose says they are 'due to its reduced size'; getting that wrong would let them stack with another size change.

effects.target: fort

As reduce person, except that it affects one humanoid creature per caster level, no two of them more than 30 feet apart. Each drops one size category with the space, reach and equipment changes that follow from it.

reduce-person-mass.notes: Numbers taken from reduce person, which this spell says it functions like; only the number of targets differs.

effects.target: An improvised weapon you touch functions as the equivalent masterwork simple or martial weapon - a chair leg as a masterwork club, a butter knife as a masterwork dagger, a pitchfork as a masterwork trident - without changing shape or appearance at all.

refine-improvised-weapon.notes: Masterwork quality is a property of the item, not a bonus on the wielder's sheet; writing it as a +1 combat_mod would stack it with a real masterwork weapon.

effects.target: Cast as an immediate action, and usable as a reaction to an attack so long as you act before the attack's result is revealed: one creature within range gains a deflection bonus to AC equal to half your caster level, lasting until the beginning of your next turn.

reflexive-barrier.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the bonus is 'equal to half your caster level' and combat_mod's amount is a fixed signed integer, so any number written here would be the number for one particular caster level. Printed duration is 'until the beginning of your next turn', which is 1 round in the schema's terms.

effects.target: A specially prepared object is charged and must then be given willingly to a creature along with a command word. When that creature speaks the word while rending or breaking the item (a standard action), it and everything it wears and carries up to its heavy load - plus a familiar or animal companion touching it - is transported instantly to your abode from any distance on the same plane. No one else is carried along. You may instead choose at casting that the breaking transports YOU to within 10 feet of the item's possessor, in which case you get a general sense of their location and situation and have no choice about being pulled there.

refuge.notes: Teleportation; nothing in the vocabulary moves a creature.

effects.target: Brings back a creature dead no more than 1 week whose soul is free and willing to return - a willing subject gets no save. Any small portion of the body that was part of it at death is enough. Over 1 hour the magic builds an entirely new young adult body from the elements at hand; all physical ills and afflictions are repaired. The creature keeps its class abilities, feats, skill ranks, class, base attack bonus, base saves and hit points.

Roll d% on the incarnation table for the new race, then strip the subject's old racial ability adjustments and apply the new ones: 01 bugbear (Str +4, Dex +2, Con +2), 02-13 dwarf (Con +2), 14-25 elf (Dex +2, Con -2), 26 gnoll (Str +4, Con +2), 27-38 gnome (Str -2, Con +2), 39-42 goblin (Str -2, Dex +2), 43-52 half-elf (Dex +2), 53-62 half-orc (Str +2), 63-74 halfling (Str -2, Dex +2), 75-89 human (Con +2), 90-93 kobold (Str -4, Dex +2, Con -2), 94 lizardfolk (Str +2, Con +2), 95-98 orc (Str +4), 99 troglodyte (Dex -2, Con +4), 100 GM's choice. The creature gains every ability of its new form - movement modes and speeds, natural armour, natural attacks, extraordinary abilities - but does not automatically speak its language.

The subject gains two permanent negative levels, or, if it is 1st level, 2 points of Constitution drain instead - and cannot be reincarnated at all if that would take its Constitution to 0 or lower. A character who died with spells prepared has a 50% chance of losing each; a spontaneous caster has a 50% chance of losing each unused slot. Cannot return a creature turned undead or killed by a death effect, nor any construct, elemental, outsider or undead; it CAN return one that died of old age. Wish or miracle restores the original form.

reincarnate.notes: The ability adjustments belong to a randomly rolled race, so no ability_mod can name them - the whole table is carried in prose. As with raise dead, the 2 Constitution drain applies only to a 1st-level subject and would be wrong applied to every one.

effects.target: disguise
effects.note: only on checks to impersonate the chosen creature; a penalty may still apply for being the wrong race

effects.target: As reincarnate, except that you can make the new body resemble a particular creature, matching its age category and sex and rerolling any race result of the wrong size category. The spell automatically leaves you a small piece of the creature's new body, usually a lock of hair, useful for scrying.

reincarnate-spy.notes: Bonus type is not stated, so untyped.

effects.target: A touched weapon or suit of armour with the fragile quality is not treated as fragile for the duration. An ordinary weapon or armour instead gains the masterwork quality for the duration and has its hardness doubled; masterwork or magical armour and weapons simply have their hardness doubled.

reinforce-armaments.notes: Item qualities and hardness belong to the object rather than to a creature's sheet; damage_reduction is a creature's, not an item's hardness.

effects.target: As reinforce armaments, except that you divide the duration into 10-minute intervals among any number of touched weapons and suits of armour.

reinforce-armaments-communal.notes: The emitted duration is the total pool before it is divided among the objects, which the schema has no way to express.

effects.target: fascinated
effects.note: allies in the cone only

effects.target: flat-footed
effects.note: allies in the cone stop counting as flat-footed even if they have not acted yet

effects.target: an ally lying prone may stand up as an immediate action, provoking attacks of opportunity as normal
Sleeping allies in the cone wake immediately.

The remaining duration of any effect making an ally confused, frightened, paralyzed, slowed or stunned is reduced by 1d4 rounds, rolled separately for each ally; an effect reduced to 0 rounds or fewer ends.

reinvigorating-wind.notes: Waking a sleeper is narrated rather than remove_condition 'unconscious', because unconscious covers being at negative hit points too and removing it would be far stronger than the spell. Shortening a condition's remaining duration by 1d4 rounds has no type in the vocabulary - remove_condition would end those five conditions outright, which the spell does not do.

effects.target: Once per round phantom hands load the touched ranged weapon or firearm with conjured ammunition. The ammunition counts as magical for overcoming damage reduction and for attacking incorporeal creatures, but is otherwise standard for its type. It ceases to exist 1 round after it leaves the weapon, or when the spell ends, whichever is sooner.

reloading-hands.notes: Conjures ammunition; no creation type exists, and the magic-for-DR property belongs to the ammunition rather than to a creature.

effects.target: Any object you can hold in one hand counts as a coin-sized object for Sleight of Hand checks to palm it or make it disappear, though you can have only one such item per caster level hidden on you at a time. The objects' actual sizes do not change.

remarkable-legerdemain.notes: Changes what a Sleight of Hand check is made against rather than adding to the check, so no skill_mod applies - a bonus would be a number the spell never states.

effects.target: You specify a distance and direction and receive a psychic impression of that location rather than its visual appearance, so it cannot be used to set up teleport - a fey-held forest might read as a city in the trees, a forbiddance-warded palace as a dark fortress in chains. Throughout the 1-hour casting your real body is unconscious and helpless and you are unaware of its surroundings.

remote-viewing.notes: Divination; the caster's own helplessness during casting is a cost, not an effect applied to a target, so no apply_condition is emitted.

effects.target: Cures blindness OR deafness, your choice, whether the cause is normal or magical. It does not restore eyes or ears that have been lost, but does repair damaged ones. Counters and dispels blindness/deafness.

remove-blindness-deafness.notes: The spell cures one of the two, chosen by the caster. Emitting remove_condition for both blinded and deafened would cure both from one casting, which is a stronger spell than the one printed.

effects.target: Removes curses from a touched creature or object. Against a creature, make a caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against the DC of each curse on it; each success removes that curse. It does not lift the curse from a cursed shield, weapon or suit of armour, but a successful caster level check does let the afflicted creature remove and discard the item. Counters and dispels bestow curse.

remove-curse.notes: The roll is the caster's caster level check against an unknown DC, not a save the target makes, so it is not a save_gate.

effects.target: Cures every disease the subject is suffering from, one caster level check (1d20 + caster level) against each disease's DC, each success curing that disease. It also kills some hazards and parasites, green slime among them. Being instantaneous, it does nothing to prevent reinfection later.

remove-disease.notes: Disease is not a condition in the vocabulary, and the cure is gated on a caster level check against a DC the spell does not know.

effects.target: saving throws against fear effects
shaken
frightened
panicked
cowering

remove-fear.notes: 'That effect is suppressed for the duration' is exactly suppress_condition, applied to the four fear conditions the vocabulary carries. Affects one creature plus one per 4 caster levels. Counters and dispels cause fear.

effects.target: Frees up to four creatures from temporary paralysis or related magic, including effects that leave a creature staggered, and what each gets depends on how many you target. Cast on one creature, the paralysis is simply negated. Cast on two, each gets another saving throw against its own affliction at a +4 resistance bonus. Cast on three or four, each gets another save at +2. It does not restore ability scores lowered by penalties, damage or drain.

remove-paralysis.notes: Only the single-target casting actually removes the condition; with two or more it grants a fresh save instead. A remove_condition spec would cure paralysis at any number of targets, which is wrong three casts in four.

effects.target: con
effects.note: drain caused by radiation only; this spell cannot restore ability damage or drain from any other source

effects.target: str
effects.note: drain caused by radiation only; this spell cannot restore ability damage or drain from any other source

effects.target: Removes all ongoing primary and secondary radiation effects on one target if you succeed at a caster level check against a DC equal to the Fortitude DC of the radiation effect. Cast on an area instead, it clears radiation from a 20-foot radius around the point you touch. It cannot neutralise naturally radioactive material, and while such material remains the radiation may return.

remove-radioactivity.notes: The two 1d4 restorations are stated plainly with dice, so they convert. ability_restore does not distinguish restoring drain from healing damage; the prose says drain, and the note records it.

effects.target: As remove radioactivity, except that it cures ALL ability damage and drain the target has taken from radioactivity, not 1d4 of each.

You can also deplete a radioactive object, though touching it exposes you to at least 1 round of its radiation. Succeed at a caster level check against DC 5 + the Fortitude DC of the radiation effect and the object stops emitting radiation - permanently rendering a nuclear reactor or atomic warhead inert and harmless.

remove-radioactivity-greater.notes: 'All' damage and drain with no dice given, and ability_restore requires dice - the 1d4 from the lesser spell would be the wrong number here, so it is narrated.

effects.target: saving throws against disease, nausea and sickened effects
nauseated
sickened

remove-sickness.notes: Disease has no condition in the vocabulary, so only the two conditions are suppressed and the disease half rides in the situational bonus.

effects.target: Permanently rearranges and resizes the rooms of an unoccupied building you constructed as a downtime activity, remapping it however you like as though every room were being placed for the first time. You cannot make a change that alters what a room costs to create or what benefits it provides, and the structure must stay in the same general position within its district. If you do not wholly own it, every owner must consent before casting or the spell fails immediately.

renovation.notes: Acts on downtime buildings; nothing in the vocabulary touches structures.

effects.note: plus 1 hit point per caster level, to a maximum of +5; channelled negative energy, so it heals undead

repair-undead.notes: This HEALS, despite being negative energy from a necromancy spell - the prose says 'heals 1d8 points of damage', which is the blaze of glory trap the brief names, and it is emitted as a heal. No effect on living creatures, except those healed by negative energy. The printed 'Will half (harmless)' lets an unwilling undead halve the healing; the schema has no harmless-save form, so no gate is emitted.

effects.target: Waves of invisible energy sweep down a 60-foot line, pushing every metal or stone object in the path away from you at 40 feet per round, out to the limit of the range. Fixed metal or stone objects over 3 inches across and loose objects over 500 pounds are unaffected; fixed objects 3 inches or smaller bend or break and travel with the wave. Armour, swords and the like are pushed back and drag their bearers with them - a creature can let go of a carried item, or loose a shield as a move action and drop it as a free action. Magic items with metal parts are repelled too, though an antimagic field blocks the spell. Once cast, the path is fixed and you can leave without weakening it.

repel-metal-or-stone.notes: Forced movement; nothing in the vocabulary pushes a creature or object.

effects.target: An invisible barrier in a 10-foot emanation around you holds back vermin. Vermin with fewer HD than one-third your level cannot cross at all. Vermin with one-third your level or more in HD can cross on a successful Will save, but crossing deals them 2d6 points of damage, and pressing against the barrier hurts enough to deter most vermin.

repel-vermin.notes: The 2d6 is taken by whichever vermin chooses to cross the barrier, at the moment it crosses - not by a target the caster picks at casting. Emitting it as a damage spec would fire it once, at the wrong time, at nobody in particular.

effects.target: Waves of energy roll down a 60-foot line in a direction you choose, pushing every wooden object in the path away from you at 40 feet per round. Firmly fixed wooden objects over 3 inches across are unaffected, loose ones are not; fixed objects 3 inches or smaller splinter and travel with the wave. Wooden shields, spears, hafts, arrows and bolts are pushed back and drag their carriers along - a creature can let go, or loose a shield as a move action and drop it as a free action, and a spear set to resist the movement splinters. Magic items with wooden parts are repelled too, though an antimagic field blocks the spell. Once cast, the path is fixed.

repel-wood.notes: Forced movement; nothing in the vocabulary pushes a creature or object.

effects.target: Reconstructs the past events that left the tracks you are using as the spell's focus, playing them out in real time forward or in reverse depending on which way you follow the trail, though never clearly enough to identify a creature exactly. You may make Survival checks to follow tracks as part of concentrating. Only events connected to those tracks appear, and anything that left no trace you could detect - a creature under pass without trace, say - is simply absent from what you see.

replay-tracks.notes: Printed duration is 'concentration, up to 1 hour/level'; concentration is emitted and the per-level cap recorded here.

effects.target: Replenishes a ki pool: you regain 2 ki points if you are the target, another creature regains 1. It cannot take a pool above its maximum, and does nothing at all to a creature without a ki pool.

replenish-ki.notes: Restores a class resource; the vocabulary has no resource-pool type.

effects.target: You recount one piece of knowledge you hold, up to 50 words, and it vanishes utterly from your mind - you may not even notice the gap, which the spell patches over with indistinct haze. This defeats detect thoughts, discern lies, zone of truth and similar spells, though careful questioning may expose the hole or the fact that your memory was tampered with. Only break enchantment, psychic surgery, limited wish, miracle or wish can restore it. Repressing the memory of a magical compulsion does not remove the compulsion, and procedural memory behind your skills and class abilities is untouched.

repress-memory.notes: Memory alteration on the caster; nothing in the vocabulary expresses it.

effects.target: Casts a creature of your own faith out of the religion, marking it with a magical symbol visible only to the faithful, who are to withhold help but not to persecute it for the mark.

The target is no longer affected by helpful spells cast by the faithful and always counts as an enemy for spells cast by them - cure light wounds from a member of your faith does nothing to it, and a friendly cleric's prayer penalises rather than aids it.

If the target is a divine spellcaster, in a prestige class of your faith, or has any ability by virtue of belonging to your faith, it cannot use those abilities while the mark stands: a paladin of your faith loses paladin spells, lay on hands and its other class abilities. Joining another faith restores the abilities but the mark stays visible to yours.

If the target committed no act or misdeed against your faith, the spell rebounds and afflicts YOU instead, even if you believed the charges. The mark can be removed as any other curse; a member of your faith can break it with atonement on a successful caster level check against your caster level, and remove curse likewise requires a caster of your faith and a caster level check.

reprobation.notes: The backlash lands on the CASTER when the accusation is false - written in its own narrative so a reader cannot mistake it for something the target suffers.

effects.target: The touched creature sweats a foul liquid. Any creature that deals damage to it with a bite attack or the swallow whole ability must succeed at a Fortitude save against this spell's DC or be nauseated until the end of that creature's next turn. Once a creature has been nauseated by this spell, each later failed save gives it the sickened condition until the end of its next turn instead.

repugnant-taste.notes: Retributive: the save and the nausea fall on whoever bites the spell's target. A save_gate here would make the engine nauseate the warded creature itself, which is precisely backwards - this is the thorn body defect in condition form.

effects.target: will
effects.note: made by any creature inside the field when you cast, or entering it afterwards

on_failure.target: The creature is unable to move any closer to you for the duration. It is otherwise unrestricted: it can fight other creatures, cast spells and shoot you with ranged weapons, and if you close to within its reach it may make melee attacks against you. It is never forced back, and if it moves away and turns around it still cannot approach while it remains in the area.

repulsion.notes: You set the field's radius at casting, up to 10 feet per caster level. A movement prohibition has no type in the vocabulary - it is not a condition and not a speed change.

effects.target: Touching a footprint gives you a clear mental image of whatever made it, exactly as it looked at that moment - telling features and expressions, gear, anything it was carrying. A horse's hoofprint shows the horse and whoever was riding it.
ref

on_failure.target: A globe of shimmering force 1 foot in diameter per caster level closes around the creature, which must be small enough to fit, and holds it for the duration. It functions as a wall of force except that dispel magic negates it. The subject can breathe normally inside, and the sphere cannot be moved by anyone outside it or by the struggles of whoever is within.

resilient-sphere.notes: Containment; not a condition, and nothing in the vocabulary imprisons.

effects.target: cmd
effects.note: against disarm attempts only

effects.target: saving throws against effects that cause you to drop something you are holding
cmb
effects.note: only to initiate a grapple, maintain a grapple, or pin a foe

effects.target: Any enemy you grapple takes a -2 penalty on attempts to break the grapple and to escape it with Escape Artist.

Any weapon that strikes you sticks fast unless its wielder succeeds at a Reflex save against this spell's DC, and can then only be pulled free with a Strength check at that same DC. Unarmed strikes and natural weapons are unaffected.

resinous-skin.notes: The -2 lands on an enemy's sheet rather than the caster's, so it is narrated. The weapon-sticking save is made by the attacker, not by the caster, which is why it is not a save_gate.

effects.target: As resist energy, except that you divide the duration into 10-minute intervals among any number of creatures touched. Each protected creature ignores the chosen energy type's damage up to the rating resist energy grants at your caster level.

resist-energy-communal.notes: The energy type is chosen at casting and the rating steps with caster level, neither of which a resistance spec can hold - its target and amount are both fixed values. The parent spell resist energy carries the numbers.

effects.target: If the target does not eat on the day this is cast, the DC to avoid nonlethal damage from starvation the following day does not increase by 1. The spell fails outright unless the target has already attempted at least one Constitution check to avoid starvation.

resist-starvation.notes: Stops a DC from rising rather than adding a bonus to a check - situational_mod would put +1 on the target's roll, which is a different rule with a different result against a fixed DC.

effects.target: fort
ref
will

resistance.notes: '+1 resistance bonus on saves' means all three, and the bonus type is named outright. Can be made permanent with permanency.

effects.target: A touched magic weapon or suit of armour of up to 25 pounds per caster level becomes up to two size categories larger or smaller. If the spell ends while resized armour is worn, the armour falls off harmlessly. Growth halts just short of any point where the item would become too large for the space holding it. Permanency for 7,500 gp fixes the object at one chosen size within two steps of its original.

resize-item.notes: Resizes an object; no size-change type exists, and size bonuses would be about a creature.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: ROUND ONE ONLY - the target saves again on each of your next two turns, with the effects below

on_success.note: half damage on a successful save, and the staggering is negated

effects.target: On the second round the target saves again: 5d6 sonic damage and stunned for 1 round, halved and the stunning negated on a success. On the third round: 10d6 sonic damage and stunned for 1d4+1 rounds, halved and the stunning negated on a success. The word has no power after the third round even if the duration is extended.

resonating-word.notes: Three rounds of escalating damage. Only round one is converted, with the note saying so; the vocabulary has no repeating-damage type and the amounts differ per round, so rounds two and three are narrated rather than folded into one number. No per-level scaling in this spell, so no scaling block.

effects.target: ref

on_failure.target: A creature wielding a metal weapon takes a -1 penalty on attack rolls; a creature using metallic tools takes -1 on the associated skill checks; a creature in metal armour has its armour check penalty worsened by 1. These penalties grow by 1 at caster level 8th and every 4 caster levels after, to a maximum of -4 at 16th. An item must be primarily metal to be affected - studded leather or padded armour with spikes is not. A creature made of metal takes the penalty on attack rolls, damage rolls, skill checks AND Reflex saves.

resounding-clang.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the penalty is -1 at low level and steps to -4 by 16th, and no mod type holds a caster-level-dependent amount. Writing -1 would be right for a 7th-level caster and wrong for every one above, so the whole scheme is narrated.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature is silenced as the silence spell. The effect covers the whole creature but does not reach beyond it, and it is one-way: sound from outside can still enter the creature's space.

respectful-quiet.notes: Affects any number of creatures in a 30-foot burst. Silence has no condition in the vocabulary, so it is narrated while the +10 Stealth converts cleanly.

effects.target: Creates a towering mansion up to 300 feet on a side and one storey tall per 4 caster levels, laid out and decorated to an image you hold while casting, with the accoutrements of whatever purpose you imagine for each room. Mundane furniture and fixtures work normally inside but cease to exist if carried out; no fixture creates magical effects, though magic items brought in work normally. It holds the same foodstuffs and servants as a mage's magnificent mansion.
Every exterior door and window carries an alarm spell, each audible or mental as you choose and each with its own distinct sound or sensation so you know at once which was used.

It must be raised on a plot free of other structures and adapts to the terrain, working around ponds or rock spires and reaching foundations through snow or sand to solid ground; it cannot be created on water or any nonsolid surface. On a solid but unstable surface such as swamp or shaking ground there is a 10% chance each day that it begins to sink or collapse. It harms no one when it appears and cannot be created among a crowd or in a densely populated area; anyone caught inside ends up unharmed within the finished mansion.

resplendent-mansion.notes: Creation; nothing in the vocabulary builds a structure.

effects.target: Curses a dead creature so that its spirit cannot return. Anyone casting a spell to communicate with it, return it to life, or make it undead must succeed at a caster level check against DC 11 + your caster level. Cannot be dispelled, but remove curse or break enchantment negates it.

rest-eternal.notes: The DC is rolled against by a future caster, not by the dead target, so it is not a save_gate.

effects.target: A cloak you are wearing becomes a canvas tent big enough for four Medium creatures, pitched in a flat area next to you - the spell simply fails if there is no such area. A creature resting inside regains 1 hit point for each hour it rests, on top of the normal benefits of resting, and a fatigued creature that rests inside for 1 hour loses the fatigued condition, though no creature can shed fatigue more than once per casting. The tent reverts to a cloak when the spell ends, and the spell ends immediately if the tent is moved.

restful-cloak.notes: 1 hit point per hour of rest is healing that repeats on a timer and only while the creature stays put - a heal spec would grant it once at casting. The fatigue removal is likewise conditional on an hour's rest, so remove_condition would fire too early.

effects.target: Cast immediately before resting on one creature per caster level. A subject that completes a full night's rest regains hit points as though it had had a full day of bed rest - twice its character level - and one that completes a full day's rest regains three times its character level. Any significant interruption, such as being woken, prevents all healing that night and ends the spell for that subject. All of this counts as natural healing and does nothing for effects that require magical healing.

restful-sleep.notes: The healing is a multiple of the subject's character level, which heal's dice field cannot express, and it only lands after a completed rest. Printed duration is '8 hours or 24 hours' depending on which rest is taken, so no single duration is emitted.

effects.target: The spell lies dormant for up to 1 hour per caster level until you are reduced to one-quarter hit points or fewer. Nothing happens until then, and if it expires or is dispelled untriggered there are no ill effects at all.

When it triggers you immediately gain a +4 enhancement bonus to Constitution and Strength, damage reduction 5/-, the benefits of haste, and healing of 4d8 points + 1 per caster level (maximum +25) - enough to save you from an otherwise mortal wound, though not from death by massive damage or from any cause other than hit point loss. The transformation also deals you 1d4 points of Intelligence damage and 1d4 points of Wisdom damage. These advantages last 1 round per caster level.

When the transformation ends it leaves you exhausted and deals 1d4 points of Constitution damage. If this is the second resurgent transformation to expire on you within 24 hours, it deals a further 1d4 Constitution damage and then kills you from system shock unless you succeed at a DC 15 Fortitude save, made after that Constitution damage is applied.

resurgent-transformation.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: everything here is DELAYED behind a trigger - dropping to a quarter hit points - and the schema has no way to say 'when X happens'. Emitting the +4s, the DR and the 4d8 healing as effects would grant all of them the instant the spell is cast, when the spell's whole point is that they wait. The emitted duration is the dormant window; once triggered the benefits run 1 round per caster level instead.

effects.target: As raise dead, but restores life and complete strength to any dead creature regardless of the state of the remains, so long as some small portion of the body that was part of it at death survives - the dust left by disintegrate counts. The creature can have been dead up to 10 years per caster level, and returns at full hit points, vigour and health with no loss of prepared spells.

The subject gains one permanent negative level, exactly as if drained by an energy-draining creature. A 1st-level subject instead takes 2 points of Constitution drain, and cannot be resurrected at all if that would reduce its Constitution to 0 or lower.
Can return someone killed by a death effect, or someone turned undead and then destroyed. Cannot return anyone who died of old age, nor any construct, elemental, outsider or undead.

resurrection.notes: One negative level here, not raise dead's two. The 2 Constitution drain applies only to a 1st-level subject, so it is not written as an ability_drain spec that would hit every subject.

effects.target: If a creature successfully takes the cursed item while you hold, wear or wield it, that creature must attempt a Will save or become fatigued, and must save again at the end of its turn every round it does not return the item to you. A second failed save makes it exhausted. While it is actively working to return the object its exhaustion is reduced to fatigue. Neither condition can be removed by effects that normally remove them, though immunity to fatigue and exhaustion works as usual. The curse ends with remove curse or when the item comes back to you, and you can have the spell on only one item at a time.

retributive-reparations.notes: Retributive: the save and the two conditions fall on whoever steals the item, while the spell's stated target is the OBJECT. A save_gate would be aimed at the object, and apply_condition would fatigue the wrong creature.

effects.target: Cast on a nonliving item of 1 pound or less whose longest dimension is 6 inches or less, while holding it. Thereafter, speaking a word you set at casting and snapping your fingers brings the item instantly into your hand from anywhere within long range. The spell fails if the item is in another creature's possession.

retrieve-item.notes: Summoning an object to hand; no teleportation or creation type exists.

effects.target: You receive psychic impressions of past events at your current location: the last hour during your first minute of concentration, the hour before that during the second minute, and so on back. If a psychically traumatic or turbulent event falls in the period you are reading, you must succeed at a concentration check - DC 20, 30 or 40 by severity - or lose the spell. From caster level 13th you may instead scan longer intervals with correspondingly less detail: 1 week per minute at 13th-15th, 1 year per minute at 16th-18th, and 1 century per minute at 19th and above, until only the most major events stand out.

retrocognition.notes: Printed duration is 'concentration, up to 1 minute/level'; concentration is emitted and the per-level cap recorded here.

effects.target: The target thrown weapon acts as though it had the returning weapon special ability, flying back to the thrower after an attack. This spell can serve as the prerequisite for crafting that special ability.

returning-weapon.notes: Grants a weapon special ability to an item; the vocabulary describes creatures' sheets, not item properties.

returning-weapon-communal.notes: The printed text is identical to returning weapon apart from the target line, which is where the 'any number' lives.

effects.target: A 40-foot-radius area draws out creatures' emotion auras: everyone inside glows constantly in colours matching their current overall emotional state, clearly visible to anything that can see them, and keeps glowing for 1d4 rounds after leaving. Emotionless creatures, and creatures the spell does not affect, glow a dull purple while inside.

reveal-emotions.notes: Divination that makes information visible; no numeric effect at all.

revelation.notes: VOCABULARY GAP: the bonus is 'equal to your caster level (maximum +10)', and situational_mod's amount is a fixed integer, so any value written would be right at exactly one caster level.

revenant-armor.notes: Everything is DELAYED behind the wearer falling unconscious, and the schema cannot say 'when X happens'. Printed duration is '1 day/level or 1 hour/level (see text)' without the text saying which applies to which state, so no duration is emitted rather than guessing one.

effects.target: Gravity reverses in up to one 10-foot cube per caster level: unattached objects and creatures in the area fall upward, reaching the top in 1 round. effects.target: Tears a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-deep extradimensional hole up to 5 feet long per caster level in a horizontal surface. Because it opens into the Abyss it does not displace the material beneath or give access to anything below - it works as well on a ship's deck as on a dungeon floor. Unattended objects and structures the rift can fully engulf simply fall in. The walls are lined with razor blades and have a Climb DC of 25.

Any creature in the rift, starting the round it enters, takes a further 6d6 points of damage per round from the Abyssal environs - even if merely climbing or flying inside - with the type rolled randomly each round from acid, bludgeoning, cold, electricity, fire, piercing, slashing or sonic. A Reflex save each round halves that round's damage.
When the spell ends the rift snaps shut and violently expels everyone still inside: they take DOUBLE the environs damage that round and are knocked prone on the surface above.

At any point you may spend a standard action to close the rift early and summon Abyssal denizens instead, expelling anyone inside as above. Choose one bebilith, one vrock, 1d3 shadow demons, 1d3 succubi, 1d4+1 babaus, or 1d4+1 brimoraks; they are treated as summoned by summon monster VII and stay for a number of rounds equal to the rift's remaining duration.

rift-of-ruin.notes: Only the 6d6 FALLING damage converts: it lands on a creature that failed the save, at the moment of casting. The other 6d6 repeats every round with a randomly rolled damage type and its own save, which the vocabulary cannot say - and the closing burst is that same repeating damage doubled, so both are narrated. Falling damage has no type in 1e, hence untyped rather than an invented bludgeoning.
